title: Walsh character under a setwise flip
statement: Let $n\ge0$, let $T,S$ be subsets of the $n$ coordinates, and let $x$ be a Boolean vector of length $n$. If $x^S$ is obtained by flipping precisely the coordinates in $S$, then $\chi_T(x^S)=(-1)^{|T\cap S|}\chi_T(x)$.
hypotheses_covered: $T$ and $S$ are subsets of the $n$ coordinates
$x$ is a Boolean vector of length $n$
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and equip $\{0,1\}^n$ with its uniform probability measure; write $\mathbb E$ for uniform expectation. For $S\subseteq[n]$, put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for real cube functions $h$. For $S\subseteq[n]$, let $x^S$ be the bit vector obtained by flipping exactly the coordinates in $S$. For all $S,T\subseteq[n]$ and $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, $\chi_T(x^S)=(-1)^{|T\cap S|}\chi_T(x)$.
